title: Volumetric Fog, on screen position mismatch.
body:
### Tested versions

I discovered this issue on Godot 4.6.3 Steam release. But I have tested it on 4.7rc1, 4.6.4rc4, 4.5, 4.4 and 4.2.

### System information

Godot v4.7.rc1 - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9649) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads) - 31.74 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The issue found is that volumetric fog seems to be disconnected from world and screen position. This originally came from working on a VR game with needed volumetric fog, but I quickly found the effect broken, more than what is shown on flat screen.

Example of what happens up close, the point of origin from this lights volumetric fog seems to drift away from where it actually is.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6b08fc5-e8c2-4a77-a394-54bdba4cc612

This one is more of a nitpick but you can see the separation of the light shaft and also you can see the light shaft overlap geometry.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/567c1245-7dc4-4dcb-9136-955fd9da388a

Additional note, while in VR the Volumetric Fog is completely broken and the effect we see here is amplified.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an empty 3D scene and add in an Omni Light and an Environment with Volumetric Fog turned on.
2. To make the effect more noticable, make the background black, set the Volumetric Fog Length to 10m and Detail Spread to 6.0. Additionally you can go to project settings and set the Volume Size to 256 and Volume Depth to 256 and Use Filter to off, note these are extremely high quality settings but makes the issue more easily seen.
3. Optionally adding in a cube that the light can cast shadows through the volumetric fog, to highlight the disconnect.
4. Last step is to take a close look at how the volumetric fog drifts from the actual scene when moving your camera around.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[VolumetricFogTesting.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28808263/VolumetricFogTesting.zip)
